static.name: Tavern Night

questions.q: A stranger at the next table is cheating at cards.

a.t: Flip the table. Cheats get what is coming.
Out-cheat him. Quietly.
Warn the poor soul he is fleecing.
Buy him a drink and learn the trick.

questions.q: The road forks at dusk. Which way?

a.t: The old forest path. It is quieter.
The king’s highway. Lamps and patrols.
Whichever leads to the ruins on my map.
Toward the music drifting over the hill.

questions.q: A locked door stands between you and what you came for.

a.t: Shoulder it open.
Pick the lock.
Study the markings on the frame first.
Knock. Someone always answers.

questions.q: A beaten enemy drops their sword and begs for mercy.

a.t: Granted. And I will see to that wound.
Granted. For a price.
That is for the magistrate to decide.
I walk away. The wilds can judge them.

questions.q: Your friends would call you…

a.t: The strong one.
The clever one.
The kind one.
The trouble.

questions.q: In a dusty cellar you find a book that whispers your name.

a.t: Open it. Obviously.
Burn it before it gets ideas.
Find a buyer. Whispering books fetch a fortune.
Bury it deep in the woods.

questions.q: The first real gold in your purse goes on…

a.t: A better blade.
A round for the whole tavern.
A rare and slightly forbidden tome.
The shrine’s poor box.

questions.q: Your turn on night watch. You pass the hours…

a.t: Running sword drills.
Listening to the forest breathe.
Working on a new song.
In quiet prayer.

questions.q: The plan has fallen apart. Now what?

a.t: I am the plan now.
Good thing I brought a second plan.
Improvise. It is more fun this way.
Get everyone out alive. Nothing else matters.

questions.q: A festival fills the town square. Where are you?

a.t: In the wrestling ring, taking all comers.
Slipping through the crowd, unnoticed.
On the stage.
At the edge of it, with the falconer’s birds.

questions.q: What frightens you most?

a.t: Being caged.
Being fooled.
Failing those who trust me.
Being forgotten.

questions.q: A dragon, amused, offers you a single gift.

a.t: Strength no one can match.
The secrets of magic.
A voice no one can refuse.
The speech of beasts and birds.

Barbarian.blurb: Fury given legs. You hit hard, shrug off harder, and think later.
Barbarian.gear: furs, a heavy greataxe, bare scarred arms
strengths: You are the strongest in the room, and you hit like a falling tree.
You shrug off knocks that would flatten anyone else.
You know the wild: its weather, its tracks and its dangers.

Bard.blurb: Words are your weapon and the room is your stage. You make everyone around you better.
Bard.gear: a lute, a feathered cap, a colorful doublet
strengths: You can talk your way out of almost anything.
Give you a song or a story and the whole room is yours.
You lie beautifully when the truth will not do.

Cleric.blurb: Faith made practical. You mend the wounded and stand firm when it counts.
Cleric.gear: chain and tabard, a mace, a glowing holy symbol
strengths: You mend wounds and get fallen friends back on their feet.
You can tell what someone feels, whatever they say.
You know the gods, their rites and what offends them.

Druid.blurb: The wild speaks and you answer. Storm, root and claw are yours to call.
Druid.gear: a gnarled staff, a cloak of leaves and hide, antler charms
strengths: Beasts trust you, and many will do as you ask.
You know every root, track and turn of the weather.
Out of doors, very little escapes your notice.

Fighter.blurb: Steel, drilled until it is instinct. You hold the line so others can shine.
Fighter.gear: chain mail, a longsword, a battered shield
strengths: You are the best with a blade, and you hold the line.
Strong enough to climb it, lift it or break it down.
One hard look from you ends most arguments.

Monk.blurb: Stillness, then lightning. Your body is the only weapon you need.
Monk.gear: simple wrapped robes, bare fists, a quarterstaff
strengths: You are faster than anyone expects, and you never lose your balance.
You move without a sound when you choose to.
You read a person’s mood before they speak.

Paladin.blurb: An oath in shining plate. You protect the weak and smite what threatens them.
Paladin.gear: polished plate, a longsword, a heraldic shield
strengths: You shield your friends, and you are very hard to knock down.
People believe you, because you mean what you say.
You can tell an honest face from a false one.

Ranger.blurb: Tracker, hunter, scout. Nothing crosses the wilds without you knowing.
Ranger.gear: a hooded forest cloak, a longbow, a quiver
strengths: You can follow any trail and never lose your way.
You see and hear trouble long before it sees you.
With a bow in your hands, you rarely miss.

Rogue.blurb: Quick, quiet and clever. You win by being where nobody expects you.
Rogue.gear: dark leathers, a hood, a pair of daggers
strengths: You slip in and out without ever being seen.
Locks and pockets open for your quick fingers.
You lie with a perfectly straight face.

Sorcerer.blurb: Magic is in your blood, and it does not always ask permission.

attacks.hint: Next to you, or thrown 20 feet

Sorcerer.gear: travel-worn finery, crackling arcane energy around the hands
strengths: Magic comes naturally to you, and it hits hard.
You know a spell when you see one, and what it is likely to do.
You can charm people or frighten them, as the moment needs.

Warlock.blurb: You made a bargain for power. The terms were… flexible.

attacks.hint: Next to you, or thrown 20 feet

Warlock.gear: dark robes, an old tome on a chain, a faint eerie glow
strengths: You know dark and secret magic that others would rather not.
You can make people believe things that are not so.
You are unsettling when you want to be, and people back down.

Wizard.blurb: A scholar of the impossible. Fragile, yes, until the spellbook opens.

attacks.hint: Next to you, or thrown 20 feet

Wizard.gear: scholar’s robes, a spellbook, a staff
strengths: You know more about magic than anyone at the table.
You remember old tales, names and dates just when they matter.
You work out puzzles and find the clue others missed.

rings on every finger, none of them matching
a crooked grin and one chipped tooth
ink-stained fingers and a quill behind one ear
a red silk scarf knotted at the throat
a necklace of mismatched keys
boots far too fine for the rest of the outfit
a falcon feather tucked into a braid
burn-scarred knuckles wrapped in linen

eyes that never stop counting the exits

a sprig of rosemary pinned to the collar

ai.style: Character portrait in the tradition of a classic fantasy tabletop roleplaying game player's handbook illustration: realistic painterly digital oil painting with visible confident brushwork, dramatic warm candle-like key light with a cool rim light, rich earthy palette with deep jewel accents, believable anatomy, costume in renaissance-fair fabrics (linen, wool, tooled leather, brass buckles). Waist-up, three-quarter view, the figure centered with space above the head. Behind the figure a loose watercolor and ink wash with splatters in muted tones that dissolves into plain light warm parchment toward every edge, so all four edges of the image are bare parchment. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no logo, no watermark.
ai.describe: You invent the look of a fantasy roleplaying character for a portrait painter. Reply with one or two sentences, 40 words at most, of concrete visual detail only: clothing, colors, one signature object, small quirks. Renaissance-fair fantasy wardrobe. The character's fixed features are listed for you: agree with every one of them and never state a different age, build, hair, mark or expression. No name, no backstory, no game terms, no quotation marks.
ai.origin: You write the opening of a fantasy roleplaying character's backstory in the voice of a storyteller at a tavern. Exactly two sentences, 45 words at most, never use "you", use the character's name. Warm, a little wry, no cliches about destiny.

text.tagline: Answer a few questions. Meet your hero. Let the dice decide the rest.
text.dm: I am the DM (I tell the story)
text.waysTitle: How do you want to start?
text.waysReplace: Your new hero takes {name}’s place as soon as they are ready.
text.fullSub: Every question, for the closest match.
text.premadeSub: No questions. Tap one and play.
text.omen: The table has taken your measure.
text.matchNote: The numbers show how closely each one fits your answers. Tap another to switch.
text.retakeText: Your new answers make a new hero, and this one will be gone.
text.pickHint: Pick the picture that feels most like your hero.
text.descHint: A patched green cloak, a crooked grin, one ear nicked in a bar fight
text.hintLive: Pick a few features, then let the painter work.
text.stale: Your choices changed. Paint another to see them.
text.painted: Painted just now by OpenAI in {s} seconds.
text.slow: The painter took too long. Try again.
text.failed: The painter could not finish: {e} Change the description or try again.
text.toTable: Take your seat at the table
text.healthHint: how much harm you can take
text.armorHint: an attack has to roll this high to hit you
text.nudge: Tap what your hero wants to do, then roll the dice. The DM, the person telling the story, says what happens next.
text.initHint: Roll when a fight starts. Highest goes first.
text.noRoll: Dash to move twice as far, Dodge to be harder to hit, Disengage to back away safely, or Help a friend. Just say it.
text.freeNote: Whatever dice the DM asks for
text.leaveText: Your seat is freed and the table forgets your hero. Your hero stays on this phone.
text.howRoll: Press Roll, or flick the tray.
text.shakeDenied: This phone did not allow it. Check that motion is allowed for this site.
text.numberWords: One Two Three Four Five Six Seven Eight
text.minus: minus {n}, as this is not your strong suit
text.hitsSay: Tell the DM. If they say it hits, roll damage.
text.nat20: A natural 20, the best roll there is. The whole tavern cheers!
text.nat20Attack: A natural 20 always hits. Roll damage with twice the dice.
text.nat1: A natural 1, the worst roll there is. The tavern winces.
text.critPlain: A perfect hit: twice the dice
text.railHint: Pick the dice the DM asks for, by how many sides they have.
text.musicNote: Music for the title, the game and the fights
text.musicNone: This cartridge has no music yet
text.musicTable: Starts off at a table, so the phones do not play over each other
text.detailsNote: Bonuses, dice names and the full sheet, for players who know the rules
text.aiOn: AI pictures and writing are on.
text.aiDirect: AI pictures and writing are on, with your own OpenAI key.
text.aiTable: AI pictures and writing switch on when you join a DM’s table.
text.aiOff: AI pictures and writing are off. The game is complete without them.
text.dmIs: The DM is the person telling the story. Ask them for the table’s four-letter code.
text.nameHint: What should the table call you?
text.seatedAs: You are seated as {name}. Use the same name and code to come back later, or on another phone.
text.needName: Tell the table your name first.
text.needCode: A table code is four letters. Ask your DM to read it out again.
text.alreadyThere: You are already at that table.
text.joinFailed: Could not join that table. Check the code and try again.
text.endKeep: Your hero is still on this phone, so you can keep playing on your own.
text.endGone: That table is no longer there. Ask your DM for a new code.
text.tablePlays: This table is playing {scenario}. Let’s make you a hero for it.
text.leaveFailed: Could not reach the table, so you are still seated. Try again.
text.feedEmpty: Nothing here yet. What your DM shows the table will land here.
text.heroOffer: Your DM offers you a ready-made hero
text.cardRoll: Your DM wants a roll for that.
text.askWait: Your DM is still thinking about three of your ideas. Give them a moment.
text.askFailed: That did not reach the table. Try again.
text.intentHint: I climb up to the window
text.reqKicker: Your DM asks for a roll
text.reqDecide: Your DM will decide how that went.
text.reqLost: That did not reach the table. Tell your DM what you rolled.
text.reqOff: Your DM has called that roll off.
text.realBad: Type the number each die shows, from 1 to {s}.
text.healthNote: Your DM tells you when you are hurt or healed. Mark it here.
text.bondText: Pick another hero and answer one question about them. The whole table sees your answer.
text.bondNeed: Write a few words first, or skip.
text.bondSaved: Bond saved. The table can see it under Who’s here.
text.bondAdd: Add a bond with another hero
text.hookText: Why is {name} here? Pick one, or skip. Only you and your DM see it.
text.voiceText: A voice to try for {name}. It is only a suggestion.
text.roleNeeded: Nobody at your table plays one yet
text.kitTell: Tell your DM you are using: {item}
text.voteNote: Tap your choice. You can change it until your DM closes the vote.
text.voteMine: Your vote is in. Tap another to change it.
text.noteHint: A name to remember, a plan, a hunch
text.notesEmpty: Nothing here yet. Pin anything from the story, or write your own. Notes stay on this phone.
text.mapNone: Nothing is uncovered yet. Your DM opens the map as you explore.
text.tableSoundNote: The sound your DM sets behind a scene. Starts off, so the phones do not play over each other
text.tableSoundMuted: Switch Sound effects on to hear them

demo.subject: A female halfling rogue (small, about three feet tall, round friendly face, curly hair, slightly pointed ears). Typical gear: dark leathers, a hood, a pair of daggers. Required details, each one clearly visible and taking priority over the typical gear and over anything said later: age: young, barely an adult; build: lean and wiry; hair: a mass of wild curls; distinguishing mark: heavy freckles; expression: wry.
demo.describe: Barely grown, lean of frame, a riot of untamed curls. Wears ink-stained fingers and a quill behind one ear, and a patched travelling cloak the color of wet moss.
demo.origin: Merla Goodbarrel grew up in a village where everyone knows your grandmother and learned early that the quiet ones see everything. These days Merla travels as a rogue, and the stories are only getting started.

sets.describe: In the prime of life, slight of frame. Wears eyes that never stop counting the exits, and burn-scarred knuckles wrapped in linen.
sets.origin: Edmund Ashdown grew up in a market town on a muddy crossroads and learned early that a promise kept is worth more than gold. These days Edmund travels as a cleric, and the stories are only getting started.

static.name: North Pole

questions.q: At the bake-off, the team at the next table is sneaking in store-bought frosting.

a.t: Tip their table over. Cheaters never prosper.
Peek at their recipe while they are busy cheating.
Quietly tell the judges.
Bring them cocoa and ask how they got away with it.

questions.q: The cookie drops you in a snowy forest. Which way?

a.t: Into the quiet pines.
Along the path with the candy-cane lamp posts.
Toward that tower full of gears and blinking lights.
Toward the sleigh bells and singing.

questions.q: The workshop door is locked, and the cookies are inside.

a.t: Shoulder it open.
Pick the lock with a candy cane.
Read the tiny instructions carved on the frame.
Knock and sing. Someone always answers a carol.

questions.q: You catch the gingerbread thief who has been swiping sprinkles. He is very sorry.

a.t: Forgive him and share my cookie.
Forgive him. For half his sprinkles.
Rules are rules. Santa decides.
Let him go. The snow will sort it out.

questions.q: Your friends would call you…

a.t: The strong one.
The clever one.
The kind one.
The trouble.

questions.q: Under the tree sits a present with no tag. It is humming.

a.t: Open it. Obviously.
Hand it straight to Santa. Not my present.
Trade it. Mystery presents are worth a fortune.
Bury it in a snowdrift, far from town.

questions.q: You won the bake-off prize money. It goes on…

a.t: A bigger, better rolling pin.
Cocoa for the whole town.
A rare book of secret recipes.
Mittens for everyone who has none.

questions.q: It is Christmas Eve and you cannot sleep. You…

a.t: Shovel the whole street. Twice.
Sit outside and listen to the snow fall.
Practice a new carol.
Make a wish on the brightest star.

questions.q: Your gingerbread house starts collapsing in front of the judges. Now what?

a.t: Hold the roof up myself.
Good thing I baked a spare wall.
Call it a gingerbread ruin. More fun this way.
Make sure nobody gets frosting in their eye.

questions.q: The North Pole winter fair is in full swing. Where are you?

a.t: Winning the tug of war.
Slipping between stalls, sampling everything unnoticed.
On the stage.
Out back with the reindeer.

questions.q: What worries you most?

a.t: Being stuck indoors.
Being tricked.
Letting my friends down.
Being left off the list entirely.

questions.q: Santa winks and offers you one gift.

a.t: Strength to lift the whole sleigh.
To know how every toy and trick works.
A voice everyone stops to listen to.
To talk with reindeer and snow owls.

Blizzard Brawler.blurb: When the snowball fight starts, you are the avalanche.
Blizzard Brawler.gear: a thick fur vest and big red mittens, holding a giant snowball overhead
strengths: You are the strongest one here. Heavy things move when you say so.
Snow, ice and bad weather never slow you down.
Not much gets past you. You spot trouble before it lands.

Caroler.blurb: Your song can lift a whole room, or crack an icicle clean in two.
Caroler.gear: a caroler’s cape and long scarf, holding a songbook and a golden bell
strengths: You can sing or talk your way out of almost anything.
Put you in front of a crowd and the crowd is yours.
You can tell a whopper without so much as a blush.

Baker.blurb: Still a baker at heart. Your treats mend scraped knees and sagging spirits.
Baker.gear: a puffy chef hat and apron, holding a tray of softly glowing cookies
strengths: You patch people up: scraped knees, sore heads, sagging spirits.
You can tell how someone really feels, whatever they say.
Your kitchen magic packs a wallop when it has to.

Tree Tender.blurb: The evergreens whisper, and you whisper back.
Tree Tender.gear: a cloak of pine boughs woven with tiny lights, a staff topped with a glowing star
strengths: Animals trust you, and most of them will do you a favor.
You know every plant, track and weather sign in the forest.
You spot what everyone else walks straight past.

Candy Cane Knight.blurb: Peppermint armor, a striped lance and a promise to hold the line.
Candy Cane Knight.gear: armor made of red-and-white peppermint candy, a candy-cane lance and a round cookie shield
strengths: You stand in front, and whatever you guard stays guarded.
Strong enough to hold a door shut, or open one that is stuck.
One stern look from you and most trouble thinks again.

Ice Skater.blurb: You glide, you spin, and it is over before anyone blinks.
Ice Skater.gear: a sleek skating outfit with a short cape, silver ice skates, poised mid-glide
strengths: You never lose your footing: ice, rooftops, tightropes, anything.
You are quick and quiet, and gone before anyone looks round.
You read people as easily as you read the ice.

Santa.blurb: The red suit fits. You lead with a laugh and a sack full of surprises.

attacks.hint: Swing it at someone next to you

Santa.gear: a red Santa suit with white fur trim and a wide black belt, a sack of presents over one shoulder
strengths: People listen when you speak, and they usually come round.
You can tell naughty from nice just by looking.
Strong enough to haul the sack, the sleigh and a friend or two.

Sleigh Pilot.blurb: Fastest thing in the winter sky, and you never miss a rooftop.
Sleigh Pilot.gear: aviator goggles, a leather flight cap and a very long scarf streaming in the wind
strengths: You never get lost, and you always find the quick way there.
Sharp eyes: you see the rooftop long before anyone else does.
You can land without a sound when you need to.

Chimney Sneak.blurb: Down the chimney and out again before the cocoa cools.
Chimney Sneak.gear: soot-smudged dark clothes and a little eye mask, tiptoeing with a coil of rope
strengths: You get in and out of places without anyone knowing you were there.
Locks, latches and pockets open for your nimble fingers.
You can keep a perfectly straight face while telling a fib.

Frost Mage.blurb: Winter itself does what you ask. Mostly.

attacks.hint: Next to you, or thrown 20 feet

Frost Mage.gear: an icy blue cloak embroidered with snowflakes, frost magic swirling around the hands
strengths: You understand magic: what is glowing, why, and how to make it stop.
You can charm people round to your way of thinking.
One frosty stare from you and they behave.

Mischief Maker.blurb: You know every trick on the Naughty List, and a few that are not on it yet.

attacks.hint: Next to you, or thrown 20 feet

Mischief Maker.gear: a purple-and-black striped scarf, juggling lumps of coal with a sly grin
strengths: You can fool almost anyone with a trick, a fib or a straight face.
You know how magic works, most of all the kind you should not touch.
When you say “or else”, people believe you.

Toymaker.blurb: If it can be built, wound up or glued, you can finish it by Christmas Eve.

attacks.hint: Next to you, or thrown 20 feet

Toymaker.gear: a tool apron stuffed with tiny tools, holding a half-built wind-up toy
strengths: If it has gears, springs or a puzzle in it, you can work it out.
You find the clue everyone else missed.
You have read all the old stories, and you remember the useful bits.

Workshop Elf.perk: Tinker’s touch: you can fix, or jam, almost any gadget.
Workshop Elf.look: a small Christmas workshop elf with pointed ears and rosy cheeks

Reindeer.perk: Sky-hop: leap as far as you can see, then rest before the next one.
Reindeer.look: a young anthropomorphic reindeer standing upright, soft brown fur, small antlers, a big black nose

Snowman.perk: Pack it back on: fresh snow patches you up, so you can take more knocks than most.
Snowman.look: a living snowman made of three packed snowballs, with stick arms, coal eyes and a carrot nose

Gingerbread.perk: Lucky crumb: roll a 1 on the 20-sided die and you may roll again.
Gingerbread.look: a living gingerbread cookie person with white icing trim and gumdrop buttons

Nutcracker.perk: Iron jaw: you can crack, crunch or clamp almost anything.
Nutcracker.look: a living wooden nutcracker toy soldier with a painted face, a square jaw and a tall hat

Penguin.perk: Belly slide: on ice or snow you move twice as far.
Penguin.look: a small round penguin with bright eyes

Yeti.perk: Too big to bully: once a day, when a blow would knock you out, stay on your feet.
Yeti.look: a huge fluffy friendly white yeti with a pale blue face and hands

Snow Fox.perk: White on white: in falling snow you are very hard to spot.
Snow Fox.look: an anthropomorphic white arctic fox standing upright, with a big fluffy tail

Human.perk: Flour power: the cookie left you as you were, and a little better at everything.
Human.look: a human baker with flour on their cheeks

flourish: a scarf at least three times too long
one mitten red and one mitten green
a string of tiny lights that will not switch off
frosting on one eyebrow that nobody has mentioned
a bell that jingles at the worst possible moments
pockets full of sprinkles
a wooden spoon tucked in the belt like a sword
earmuffs shaped like cinnamon buns
a patched sweater with a wonky snowflake
boots that squeak with every step
a candy cane behind one ear
a tiny whisk on a necklace

actions.hint: Up the chimney, over the drift

ai.style: Character portrait as a still from a modern 3D computer-animated family feature film: stylized, appealing character design with big expressive eyes and friendly exaggerated proportions, soft detailed materials (knit wool, fur, felt, icing) with gentle subsurface glow, warm key light and a cool winter rim light, shallow depth of field. Waist-up, three-quarter view, centered, full of personality, with space above the head. Background: a softly blurred snowy North Pole village at night with warm string lights and bokeh. Wholesome, festive and funny. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no logo, no watermark.
ai.describe: You design characters for a 3D animated Christmas family film set at the North Pole. Reply with one or two sentences, 40 words at most, of concrete visual detail only: outfit, colors, one signature prop, small quirks. Cute, festive and a little funny. The character's fixed features are listed for you: agree with every one of them and never state a different age, size, headwear, accessory or mood. No name, no backstory, no game terms, no quotation marks.
ai.origin: You narrate a cozy, funny animated Christmas film. The description starts with the character's name, then the two or three words for what they are now (for example "Reindeer Sleigh Pilot"). In exactly two sentences, 45 words at most, tell how they were a prize-winning cookie baker who nibbled an enchanted cookie from the C.O.O.K.I.E. Department and woke up at the North Pole as that, using those exact words for what they became and inventing no other creature. Use the name, never "you". Playful and kid-friendly.

story.alt: Four bakers lifting a cookie trophy on a small-town stage
story.text: You did it. Your team just won the town’s Christmas cookie bake-off, trophy and all.

story.alt: An open box of cookies with a glowing sealed note tucked inside
story.text: That night you open the box of winning cookies to finally taste them. Tucked inside is a note: the North Pole needs your help. It is signed by the C.O.O.K.I.E. Department, the Committee of Operatives Keeping Ingredients Enchanted.

story.alt: The bakers swept off the kitchen floor in a swirl of sparkles and snow
story.text: A prank, obviously. You all laugh and take a nibble. The kitchen starts to spin, the air smells of peppermint, and the cookie begins deciding who you really are…

extras.label: Nibble a North Pole cookie
extras.hint: The recipe has gone wrong. Roll to see how.
extras.title: Cookie side effect
extras.note: d6 · something is off with the recipe
table: Endless farts. They will not stop for a full minute.
A sneezing fit: three enormous sneezes.
A massively runny nose. Find a hankie, fast.
Hiccups that jingle like sleigh bells.
Your voice goes squeaky until your next roll.

text.tagline: Something is wrong with the Christmas cookies, and the North Pole needs its best bakers.
text.dm: I am the DM (I tell the story)
text.waysTitle: How do you want to start?
text.waysReplace: Your new hero takes {name}’s place as soon as they are ready.
text.fullSub: Every question, for the closest match.
text.premadeSub: No questions. Tap one and play.
text.omen: Snow. Sleigh bells. You open your eyes at the North Pole, and you are not quite yourself.
text.matchNote: The numbers show how closely each one fits your answers. Tap another to switch.
text.retakeText: Your new answers make a new hero, and this one will be gone.
text.pickHint: Pick the picture that feels most like your hero.
text.painting: The elves are busy on it
text.descHint: A scarf three times too long, frosting on one eyebrow, a very determined look
text.hintLive: Pick a few features, then let the artist work.
text.stale: Your choices changed. Make another to see them.
text.painted: Made just now by OpenAI in {s} seconds.
text.slow: The artist took too long. Try again.
text.failed: The artist could not finish: {e} Change the description or try again.
text.healthHint: how much harm you can take
text.armorHint: an attack has to roll this high to hit you
text.nudge: Tap what your hero wants to do, then roll the dice. The DM, the person telling the story, says what happens next.
text.initHint: Roll when a fight starts. Highest goes first.
text.noRoll: Dash to move twice as far, Dodge to be harder to hit, Disengage to back away safely, or Help a friend. Just say it.
text.freeNote: Whatever dice the DM asks for
text.leaveText: Your seat is freed and the table forgets your hero. Your hero stays on this phone.

checkHints.CON: Brave the cold, hold your breath

text.howRoll: Press Roll, or flick the tin.
text.shakeDenied: This phone did not allow it. Check that motion is allowed for this site.
text.numberWords: One Two Three Four Five Six Seven Eight
text.minus: minus {n}, as this is not your strong suit
text.whyAthletics: being strong as a sleigh team
text.whySurvival: knowing your way in the snow
text.hitsSay: Tell the DM. If they say it hits, roll damage.
text.nat20: A natural 20, the best roll there is. Jingle all the way!
text.nat20Attack: A natural 20 always hits. Roll damage with twice the dice.
text.nat1: A natural 1, the worst roll there is. Oh, crumbs.
text.critPlain: A perfect hit: twice the dice
text.railHint: Pick the dice the DM asks for, by how many sides they have.
text.musicNote: Carols for the title, the game and the snow fights
text.musicNone: This cartridge has no music yet
text.musicTable: Starts off at a table, so the phones do not play over each other
text.detailsNote: Bonuses, dice names and the full sheet, for players who know the rules
text.aiOn: AI pictures and writing are on.
text.aiDirect: AI pictures and writing are on, with your own OpenAI key.
text.aiTable: AI pictures and writing switch on when you join a DM’s table.
text.aiOff: AI pictures and writing are off. The game is complete without them.
text.dmIs: The DM is the person telling the story. Ask them for the table’s four-letter code.
text.nameHint: What should the table call you?
text.seatedAs: You are seated as {name}. Use the same name and code to come back later, or on another phone.
text.needName: Tell the table your name first.
text.needCode: A table code is four letters. Ask your DM to read it out again.
text.alreadyThere: You are already at that table.
text.joinFailed: Could not join that table. Check the code and try again.
text.endKeep: Your hero is still on this phone, so you can keep playing on your own.
text.endGone: That table is no longer there. Ask your DM for a new code.
text.tablePlays: This table is playing {scenario}. Let’s make you a hero for it.
text.leaveFailed: Could not reach the table, so you are still seated. Try again.
text.feedEmpty: Nothing here yet. What your DM shows the table will land here.
text.heroOffer: Your DM offers you a ready-made hero
text.cardRoll: Your DM wants a roll for that.
text.askWait: Your DM is still thinking about three of your ideas. Give them a moment.
text.askFailed: That did not reach the table. Try again.
text.intentHint: I climb up to the window
text.reqKicker: Your DM asks for a roll
text.reqDecide: Your DM will decide how that went.
text.reqLost: That did not reach the table. Tell your DM what you rolled.
text.reqOff: Your DM has called that roll off.
text.realBad: Type the number each die shows, from 1 to {s}.
text.healthNote: Your DM tells you when you are hurt or healed. Mark it here.
text.bondText: Pick another hero and answer one question about them. The whole table sees your answer.
text.bondNeed: Write a few words first, or skip.
text.bondSaved: Bond saved. The table can see it under Who’s here.
text.bondAdd: Add a bond with another hero
text.hookText: Why is {name} here? Pick one, or skip. Only you and your DM see it.
text.voiceText: A voice to try for {name}. It is only a suggestion.
text.roleNeeded: Nobody at your table plays one yet
text.kitTell: Tell your DM you are using: {item}
text.voteNote: Tap your choice. You can change it until your DM closes the vote.
text.voteMine: Your vote is in. Tap another to change it.
text.noteHint: A name to remember, a plan, a hunch
text.notesEmpty: Nothing here yet. Pin anything from the story, or write your own. Notes stay on this phone.
text.mapNone: Nothing is uncovered yet. Your DM opens the map as you explore.
text.tableSoundNote: The sound your DM sets behind a scene. Starts off, so the phones do not play over each other
text.tableSoundMuted: Switch Sound effects on to hear them
